title: Compatibility burden matrix and rollout gate automation for runtime versioning
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: Define an operationally actionable semantic versioning policy for the serving runtime that minimizes customer migration burden, supports an LTS channel with a clear delta window, and enables automated rollout gates in CI/CD. This ticket captures the compatibility burden matrix (classifying changes by consumer impact and required mitigations), the automated gating rules we will enforce in release pipelines, the client shim/adapter guidance for downstream SDKs, and the scope for an Upgrade Assistant CLI to help customers migrate.
compatibility_burden_matrix: Class A - Latent ABI/contract break (e.g., removed field in wire protocol): breaking, disallow on stable channel, allowed on next-major with migration guide and client-adapter; mitigation: automatic canary flag + adapter shim, deprecation header, 6-month LTS delta window.

Class B - Behavioral change with semantic regressions (e.g., tokenization/kv semantics that change outputs): high-risk, require cross-model/eval regression tests and a staged rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated quality gates; mitigation: rollout rollback automation + regression alerting.

Class C - Performance/resource-change (e.g., batching algorithm change, cache eviction behavior): medium-risk, allowed as minor if backwards-compatible API, must ship with opt-out flag and perf/latency dashboards; mitigation: opt-in beta channel and runtime flags.

Class D - Non-breaking additions (e.g., new optional fields, new endpoints marked experimental): low-risk, allowed on patch/minor, documented in changelog; mitigation: no runtime client changes required, but add feature flags for early testers.
Class E - Internal refactor/impl-only (no contract change): no customer impact; mitigation: standard CI + canary verification, no special customer communication needed.
rollout_gate_rules: All Class A or B changes must include a migration plan doc linked in the PR and have a migration-assistant prototype before 'merge'.
Automatic CI gates: unit tests pass, compatibility fuzzer score >= baseline, canary smoke passes in two regions, token-latency percentile regression <= 5%.
Canary policy: 2-phase canary (internal infra -> public 5% traffic) with automated monitoring: error-rate, 99th latency, and quality-regression on saved prompts.
Rollback automation: on gate failure, pipeline triggers immediate routing rollback and posts incident stub to incident channel with remediation checklist.
LTS delta window: breaking changes may be queued for the next-major but we provide a documented 'delta window' of 180 days where compatibility shims and grace headers are expected.
upgrade_tooling_scope: Upgrade Assistant CLI: dry-run mode that scans customer configs for deprecated flags, reports compatibility risk score, and can auto-generate migration patches for SDK adapters.

Client adapter guidelines: small compatibility shims shipped in SDKs to translate older wire shapes to new ones; adapters must be backward-compatible for two minor versions after a change is released.
Changelog and deprecation headers: every release must include machine-readable deprecation metadata (deprecation start, removal date, mitigation steps) in release artifacts.
Rollout dashboard: per-release view in Console showing canary progression, health metrics, and customer-facing migration status.
automation_tasks: Add 'compatibility-burden' label classifier to PR bot so PRs are preliminarily categorized by change class.
Extend CI to run compatibility fuzzer and compute a compatibility delta score that gates merges for Class A/B.
Implement automated canary orchestration in the deployment pipeline that toggles routing percentages and wires back into the Console dashboard.
Add an API to publish machine-readable deprecation metadata with each release artifact for downstream SDKs to consume.
acceptance_criteria: Documented compatibility burden matrix published to Confluence + engineering README and linked from PR template.
PR bot labels PRs with a preliminary change class with >80% accuracy on a held-out sample of recent PRs.
CI release pipeline enforces the compatibility delta score gate for Class A/B changes and can trigger automated rollback on threshold breaches.
Upgrade Assistant prototype can detect deprecated flags in 90% of sampled customer configs and propose a migration patch.
risks_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: strict gating reduces release velocity. Decision: enforce strict gates for Class A/B only; give product teams a documented fast-path review for emergency fixes.
Risk: adapter shims increase surface area and maintenance. Decision: limit official shim lifetime to two minor releases and require tests that validate shim behavior.
Tradeoff: longer LTS delta window helps customers but delays cleanup of technical debt. Decision: set delta window to 180 days with executive exceptions handled via RFC.
